The Motorola Moto G50 was released in 2021.

There is no port yet. The results below were measured with Debian 13 (arm64, systemd) on the stock bootloader and the vendor 5.4 kernel, and are meant as groundwork for a postmarketOS port. The author of this page owns the tested unit (an XT2137-2). Its screen is broken, so display and touch were never tested. All the work was done over USB and WiFi.

* [[User:Gahingwoo]]

== Users owning this device ==
{{Device owners}}

== How to enter flash mode ==
Turn the phone off, then hold {{Button|Volume Down}} and {{Button|Power}} at the same time to enter fastboot.

It is also possible to enter fastboot using <code>adb</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="shell-session">
$ adb reboot bootloader
</syntaxhighlight>

== How to unlock the bootloader ==
Enter flash mode (see [[#How to enter flash mode]]) and follow the instructions on [https://en-us.support.motorola.com/app/standalone/bootloader/unlock-your-device-a Motorola Support]. The tested unit was already unlocked, so this procedure was not tried on it.

== Installation ==
There is no postmarketOS image for this device yet. The Debian setup used for these notes is at [https://github.com/gahingwoo/debian-ibiza debian-ibiza]. To test an image without writing anything, use <code>fastboot boot boot.img</code>; a reboot then returns to the previous system. Back up <code>boot_a</code>, <code>modem*</code>, <code>modemst1</code>, <code>modemst2</code>, <code>fsg</code>, <code>fsc</code>, <code>persist</code> and the GPT first.

=== What works on Debian (vendor 5.4 kernel) ===
These results are for Debian, not postmarketOS, so the status fields in the infobox are left empty.
{| class="wikitable"
! Feature !! State !! Notes
|-
| Booting || Works || <code>fastboot boot</code> of an Android boot image v3 (kernel plus its own initramfs) with the stock <code>vendor_boot</code>. Flashing it to <code>boot_a</code> also works
|-
| USB networking || Works || configfs gadget, NCM + ACM
|-
| WiFi || Works || The firmware runs in a modem protection domain, so the modem has to boot. <code>qrtr</code>, <code>pd-mapper</code>, <code>tqftpserv</code> and <code>rmtfs</code> must be running before the modem starts, together with Android's <code>pm-service</code> and <code>cnss-daemon</code> (details below)
|-
| Bluetooth || Partly || Scanning works. Pairing and audio: untested. The firmware is loaded from userspace (details below)
|-
| Battery, charging, thermal sensors || Works || sysfs (<code>qcom_battery</code>, thermal zones)
|-
| cpufreq || Works || schedutil on both clusters
|-
| Display, touch || Untested || The screen of the tested unit is broken
|-
| GPU, audio, camera, cellular modem || Untested || Not attempted
|}

=== Things a port has to know ===
* The kernel has no <code>CONFIG_DEVTMPFS</code>, no IPC/PID/USER namespaces, no debugfs and no FHANDLE/AUTOFS. systemd treats a <code>/dev</code> that is not a mount point as fatal, so the initramfs mounts a tmpfs on the new root's <code>/dev</code> and fills it from <code>/sys/class/*</code> before <code>switch_root</code>. Units that use namespaces need <code>PrivateIPC=no</code> and similar settings.
* The bootloader needs a legacy LZ4 ramdisk. A gzip ramdisk stacked after LZ4 does not boot.
* The WiFi firmware lives in the modem. The downstream kernel drops userspace QRTR registrations made after the modem link comes up, so the QRTR services have to be running first. Run <code>rmtfs</code> on copies of <code>modemst1</code>, <code>modemst2</code>, <code>fsg</code> and <code>fsc</code>, never on the real partitions, because they hold the IMEI and RF calibration.
* <code>cnss-daemon</code> and <code>pm-service</code> are bionic binaries. They run from the read-only <code>system</code> and <code>vendor</code> partitions in a chroot, with a small <code>LD_PRELOAD</code> that fakes the property service and the SELinux calls. The board data file <code>bdwlan_ibiza_ipa.bin</code> must be visible at <code>/vendor/firmware_mnt/image</code>.
* <code>wlan.ko</code> is built with <code>PANIC_ON_BUG</code>. Never <code>rmmod wlan</code> after a failed load.
* Bluetooth has four separate problems. The host UART runtime-suspends when idle, and closing the tty drops RTS. The kernel's <code>hci_qca</code> sends a 243-byte first TLV segment that kills the chip's parser, while a 16-byte first segment works. Keep the tty open from a resident process and <code>btattach</code> to a pty.
* '''Never resize or add entries to the GPT of the UFS LUN that holds <code>super</code> and <code>userdata</code> with sgdisk.''' Afterwards the bootloader reads nothing on that LUN: <code>cid</code> and <code>imei</code> come back empty and <code>fastboot boot</code> fails with "No Media". To recover, run <code>fastboot flash partition gpt.bin</code> with the file from the stock firmware package.
* A/B slots: with no Android to call <code>markBootSuccessful</code>, the slot's retry counter drops on every boot. Either set the successful bit (bit 54 of the <code>boot_a</code> GPT attributes, rewriting both tables and their CRCs) or reset the counter with <code>fastboot set_active a</code>. <code>fastboot flash boot_a</code> resets the attributes.

=== Related work ===
Checked on 2026-10-14: pmaports has no <code>device-motorola-ibiza</code>, and no merge request or issue mentions ibiza, SM4350 or the Moto G50. A merge request for the Moto G82 5G (<code>motorola-rhodep</code>, SM6375, mainline kernel) was closed on 2026-09-30.
